pages.title: Delivery and assembly
pages.body:
Every piece is made to order in our workshop and ships in 6 to 8 weeks. Pieces marked In stock ship within 5 business days.

How delivery works

When your piece is ready, we call to agree a two-hour delivery slot. Two of our team carry it to the room you choose, assemble it and take every bit of packaging away.

Delivery and assembly is free on orders over $1,500 in the continental United States. Below that, it is a flat $95.

Before we arrive

Measure doorways, stairs and corners against the dimensions on the product page. Sofas and beds arrive with their legs off, so the depth is the number that matters most.

pages.title: Warranty and returns
pages.body:
Every sofa, bed and table frame carries a 10-year warranty against defects in materials and workmanship. Fabrics and finishes are covered for 2 years.

30 nights at home

Live with your piece for 30 nights. If it is not right, tell us and we collect it for free and refund you in full. Custom-sized pieces and textiles that have been used cannot be returned.

pages.title: Care guide
pages.body:
Oiled oak

Wipe with a damp cloth and dry straight away. Once or twice a year, rub in a thin coat of hardwax oil with a soft cloth to refresh the surface. Use coasters for hot dishes and wet glasses.

Upholstery

Vacuum cushions weekly with a soft brush and turn them over to keep their shape. Blot spills, never rub. Our covers are removable and can be dry cleaned.

pages.title: Fabric samples
pages.body:
See and feel our fabrics and finishes at home before you choose. Order up to six free samples with the form below and we post them within two business days.

Our range: linen sand, bouclé ivory, velvet rust and wool charcoal upholstery, in natural or smoked solid oak.

pages.title: Contact
pages.body: Questions about a piece, a delivery or your room? Write to us and we reply within one business day.

pages.title: Our story
pages.body:
Sotto began in a small joinery workshop with one rule: make furniture that is still in the room in thirty years.

We build in solid oak, never veneer, and join it the traditional way, with mortise and tenon instead of screws. Each board is picked by hand for its grain, so a tabletop reads as one surface.

Our upholstery is covered in natural fabrics in a calm palette, and every cover comes off, so a sofa can outlast a decade of family life.

pages.title: Showroom
pages.body:
Sit on every sofa, open every drawer and see our fabrics in daylight. Our showroom is open Thursday to Sunday, 10 am to 6 pm.

Want an hour with one of our designers? Book a visit through the contact page and bring your floor plan.

articles.title: How to measure for a sofa
articles.summary: Three numbers to check before you fall for a sofa.
articles.body:
A sofa has to fit the room, but first it has to get there. Before you order, check three numbers.

The width of the wall, minus at least 45 cm on each side so the room can breathe. The depth, which should leave 75 cm of walkway in front. And the narrowest doorway on the way in, which needs to be wider than the sofa is deep.

Every product page lists width, depth, height and seat height, and our sofas arrive with their legs off to make the turn into the room easier.

articles.title: Caring for oiled oak
articles.summary: Why we oil our oak, and the ten minutes a year it asks of you.
articles.body:
We finish our oak with hardwax oil, not lacquer. Oil soaks into the wood instead of sitting on top, so the grain stays soft to the touch and a scratch can be repaired instead of the whole top being stripped.

Day to day, a damp cloth is all it needs. Once or twice a year, rub in a thin coat of oil with a soft cloth, leave it for ten minutes and buff off the excess.

Over time the oak deepens in color. That patina is the point.

articles.title: Choosing a fabric you can live with
articles.summary: Linen, bouclé, velvet or wool: how each one wears.
articles.body:
Washed linen is cool, relaxed and gets softer with every wash. It creases, and that is part of its charm.

Bouclé is warm and textured and hides everyday marks well. Velvet has a deep color and a gentle sheen, and is surprisingly hard-wearing. Felted wool is the most durable of all and the one we recommend for homes with pets.

Not sure? Order free samples and look at them in your own light.
